```{=typst}
#question(10)[
  Define a sampling distribution and explain why it is central to statistical
  inference.

  #solution[
    The sampling distribution of a statistic is the distribution of that
    statistic over all possible samples of a given size. It links a single
    sample to the population parameter and underpins confidence intervals and
    hypothesis tests.
  ]
]
```

```{=typst}
#question(none)[
  Consider the sample mean $overline(X)$ of a random sample of size $n$.

  #part(4)[
    State the Central Limit Theorem.
    #solution[
      For large $n$, $overline(X)$ is approximately normal regardless of the
      population distribution, with mean $mu$ and variance $sigma^2 \/ n$.
    ]
  ]
  #part(4)[
    Explain how the variance of $overline(X)$ changes with $n$.
    #solution[
      The variance is $sigma^2 \/ n$, so it shrinks in proportion to $1 \/ n$.
    ]
  ]
]
```

```{=typst}
#question(7)[
  A claim states that a population mean equals 50. Briefly outline the steps of
  a hypothesis test for this claim.

  #solution[
    State $H_0: mu = 50$ and $H_1: mu eq.not 50$; choose a significance level;
    compute the test statistic; compare to the critical value (or use the
    p-value); conclude.
  ]
]
```
